info.name: NaviRoute API
info.description:
End-to-end requests for the NaviRoute backend.

Setup:
1. Import this collection and "NaviRoute Local.postman_environment.json"; select the environment.
2. Set adminEmail / adminPassword in the environment to the values the app was started with (NAVIROUTE_ADMIN_EMAIL / NAVIROUTE_ADMIN_PASSWORD).
3. Start infrastructure (docker compose up -d) and the app (mvn spring-boot:run).
4. Run the whole collection with the Collection Runner (folders 0–7; folder 8 is a manual outage test), or click through in order.

Tokens and IDs are saved automatically into collection variables. "0. Start" creates fresh users for every run.
All payments are simulated (no payment gateway).

request.description: A rider can have only one active ride (also enforced by a database constraint).
Matching is asynchronous. In the Collection Runner this request repeats (up to 10 times, 1.5 s apart) until the ride is ACCEPTED. When clicking manually, just send it again after a moment.

While BUSY the position is remembered but the driver is not matchable.
Stores the ride-completed event in the outbox_events table in the same transaction; it is published to Kafka in the background.

item.name: 8. Outbox test (manual Kafka outage)
item.description:
Manual test of the transactional outbox (Kafka outage → no lost payment). Needs the app running against docker compose.

Steps:
1. Run requests 1–4 (new ride for the same rider and driver).
2. In a terminal: docker compose stop kafka
3. Run "5. Complete ride (Kafka DOWN)" — it still succeeds immediately.
4. Run "6. Payment while Kafka is down" — expect 404 (event waiting in outbox_events).
   Optional check:
   docker exec -it naviroute-postgres psql -U ridesharing -d ridesharing_dev -c "SELECT id, status, attempts, last_error FROM outbox_events ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 3;"
5. In a terminal: docker compose start kafka
6. Run "7. Payment after Kafka is back" — retries until the payment exists (backoff can take up to a few minutes after a long outage).

Do NOT stop Kafka before step 3: requesting a ride with Kafka down can hang for up to 60 s (other events are still sent directly).
In the Collection Runner (Kafka never stopped) this folder simply runs a second normal ride.

request.description: After the first ride the driver is ONLINE near the drop-off; move them back so they are within 5 km of the pickup.
Matching is asynchronous. In the Collection Runner this request repeats (up to 10 times, 1.5 s apart) until the ride is ACCEPTED. When clicking manually, just send it again after a moment.
Before sending: docker compose stop kafka. Completion does not talk to Kafka, so it succeeds; the event waits in the outbox.

Returns 404 until then. In the Collection Runner this request repeats until the payment exists.
